stimulus.description: Mean angle of stem curvature toward the light source after 24 hours (mean ± 2SE) for each group of bean seedlings

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: A student investigates how the wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot affects the bean seedlings' response. Identify the independent variable in the investigation.
parts.model_answer: The independent variable is the wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the independent variable
required_elements: wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot
optional_phrases: the levels tested: no light (dark), red light, blue light

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the group that served as the control in the investigation, and explain why a control group is needed.
parts.model_answer: The control group was the no light (dark) group, which provides a baseline for comparison.

rubric_rows.criterion: Names the control group and states it provides a baseline/comparison for the effect of the variable

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: State a null hypothesis for the investigation.
parts.model_answer: There is no difference in the angle of stem curvature toward the light source among the groups; the wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot has no effect.

rubric_rows.criterion: States no effect or no difference in the dependent variable among the groups

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: A student claims that blue light increases the angle of stem curvature toward the light source compared with no light (dark). Using the data in the table, support the student's claim.
parts.model_answer: blue light: 41.7 ± 3.4 versus control 4.2 ± 3.2; the ±2SE intervals do not overlap, so the difference is statistically supported.

rubric_rows.criterion: Cites the group means and notes the error bars (±2SE) do not overlap (the difference is real)

stimulus.description: Mean carbon dioxide produced in 20 minutes (milliliters) ± 2SE for yeast populations at three levels of sugar concentration

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Based on the data, describe the relationship between sugar concentration and the carbon dioxide produced in 20 minutes across the three levels.
parts.model_answer: The carbon dioxide produced in 20 minutes increases across the levels (4.2, 10.8, 17.7).

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the trend using the values (or direction) from the table

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the percent change in the mean carbon dioxide produced in 20 minutes from 0.5% to 2%. Show your work.

rubric_rows.criterion: Percent change with work shown (answer)

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Using the error bars (±2SE), identify the pair of levels, if any, for which the mean carbon dioxide produced in 20 minutes is not statistically different.
parts.model_answer: Answer: none of the pairs.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the pair whose ±2SE intervals overlap (or states none) (answer)

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: A student claims that carbon dioxide produced in 20 minutes is greatest at 8%. Use the data to support the claim and describe what the error bars indicate about it.
parts.model_answer: 17.7 ± 1.68 at 8% is higher than the other levels; the ±2SE intervals do not overlap.

rubric_rows.criterion: Cites the highest mean and states what the non-overlap/overlap of error bars shows (support)
